transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-03-04
Start: 15:00 PST
Duration: ~52 minutes
Meeting title: Pioneer Analytics - postmortem + follow-up
Attendees: Alex Kim (Redwood AE), Priya Shah (Redwood SE), Marcus Lee (CSM) — John Rivera (CTO), Sara Nguyen (SRE), Ethan Park (Product)

Summary notes (auto):
- Incident on 2026-03-02 caused by KV cache eviction + quantization compatibility fallback; saw spikes in 5xx and higher latencies for ~22 minutes.
- Temporary mitigation: revert to full-precision model on affected pool, applied tighter cache TTLs.
- Long-term: improved kernel selection logic, determinism checks, add adaptive rollback policy.

Transcript:
[00:00] Alex: okay good afternoon everyone, um we wanted to walk through the postmortem action items and make sure we have owners and dates. John, can you confirm you got the incident timeline we sent?
[00:12] John: yeah we did thanks Alex. The timeline looks right to us, the spike started around 09:12 UTC and the first elevated error rates were around 09:13 then full fallback to the older shard at 09:34.
[00:27] Priya: just to add, from our side the logs show a sequence of kv cache misses then a quantized kernel fallback which caused state mismatches in the session, that's what produced a subset of 5xx errors. there were some noisy retries which made the effective load much higher.
[00:44] Sara: right and on our end the SRE team saw retry storms because our client lib retries on 429/502 by default, that amplified it. we changed the retry config during the incident but want a better default.
[01:03] Ethan: quick question, is this related to the dedicated pools or the hosted route? we were seeing it in dedicated, right?
[01:12] Alex: correct — it was on your dedicated GPU pool, the kernel selection path had a fallback that wasn't fully validated with the quantized weights. when the cache evicted prefixes it triggered the fallback path.
[01:24] John: i remember seeing a note about 'redwood optimize' recommending quantization for cost reasons, could that have pushed us into a risky config?
[01:33] Priya: the recommendation is safe in general, but the combination of short TTL on KV cache and this particular model + quant config activated a code path we hadn't exercised in our internal benchmarks. basically an edge case.
[01:49] Alex: and to be clear, customer data integrity wasn't exposed — it was availability and latency. there were no data exfiltration or privacy concerns.
[01:58] Sara: good to confirm.
[02:08] Marcus: we also want to make sure our runbooks are up to date and that the canary rollback triggers are correct so you don't have to do a manual revert.
[02:18] John: agreed. what are the short term mitigations we can take?
[02:24] Priya: short term we reverted to full-precision variant on the affected pool, increased KV TTL from 30s to 5m, and disabled that quantized fallback path for the model family. that removed the mismatch.
[02:41] Sara: that helped, but we also want an automated fallback so we don't have to manually revert.
[02:48] Priya: yes we propose an adaptive rollback policy — if error rate > 1.5% for 3 minutes AND latency p95 > x ms then revert. also add more granular tracing in the KV/cache layer.
[03:06] Ethan: can Redwood provide a sample metric dashboard we can plug into our pager?
[03:12] Alex: yes we'll share a dashboard template, and an alerting playbook.
[03:18] John: there was also a period where some proper nouns in the logs were garbled, not sure if that's the transcriber. irrelevant but just noting.
[03:26] Priya: noted — sometimes our internal traces abbreviate, but we'll make sure log names are consistent and easier to grep.
[03:35] Alex: any blockers on the remediation timeline?
[03:39] Sara: only that we need Redwood's sanitized traces to map request ids to our logs.
[03:46] Alex: absolutely, we'll redact PII and share by Friday.
[03:50] Marcus: action item — Alex to share logs; Priya to run regression with quantized variants; Marcus to update runbooks; Sara to provide load profile.
[04:05] John: what about cost impact of reverting to full precision? we need a clear estimate.
[04:11] Alex: yes we'll include cost delta in the follow-up; initial rough estimate shows ~12-18% increase for the affected pool while on full-precision. exact numbers after benchmark.
[04:23] Ethan: we also want to run an on-prem benchmark to simulate our peak traffic and verify kernel selection on our hardware. is Redwood able to support that?
[04:33] Priya: yes SE team can run an on-prem week; we'll need access to your test cluster and a brief config doc. propose week of 2026-03-16.
[04:44] Sara: that'll work if we get the instrumentation in place ahead of time.
[04:49] Alex: ok next, risk/reliability improvements longer term: make kernel selection deterministic under eviction, add unit tests for fallback paths, quantization compatibility checks in the model onboarding pipeline, and possibly a pre-flight canary for model swaps.
[05:08] John: these seem reasonable. can you provide docs on the verification steps for new model variants?
[05:14] Priya: yes we'll share the onboarding checklist and the quantization checklist.
[05:20] Ethan: also curious if SAML/SSO audit logs were involved; we saw some alert noise in our SIEM during the incident.
[05:28] Marcus: that was likely unrelated alerting — we'll correlate. but we'll add a note to the incident write-up about unrelated SIEM noise.
[05:36] Alex: okay let's go through the action items and owners one more time.
[05:40] (recap of action items)
[05:45] Alex: Alex will send sanitized traces by 2026-03-06; Priya will run regressions and share patches by 2026-03-09; Marcus will update runbook by 2026-03-07; Sara will share load profile by 2026-03-05; Redwood to draft postmortem and remediation plan by 2026-03-08.
[06:10] John: agree. we'll also plan for the on-prem benchmark the week of 2026-03-16 and identify 2 engineers to be onsite/online.
[06:20] Ethan: is there anything else?
[06:22] Alex: nothing major, we'll follow up with the doc and links.
[06:25] Sara: thanks everyone.
[06:27] (meeting ends — remainder of recording contains slide links and a short 1:1 between Alex and Marcus about contract language)

Notes on transcription: filler words and overlaps preserved; occasional mis-attribution (SE lines labeled as AE sometimes) and minor word swaps (kv vs cv). Attachments referenced: incident timeline spreadsheet (link), sanitized logs S3 link (to be provided), postmortem doc (to be drafted).

End of transcript.
